colophon: Thus ends the Sri Shani Raksha Stava.

lines.2: Having meditated on Ganapati, King Yudhishthira, the lord of dharma,
lines.3: steadfast, composed this excellent hymn to slow-moving Shani.
lines.4: Om. Of this king of Shani hymns, the seer is Sindhudvipa; the meter is gayatri;
lines.5: the deity is Sri Shanaishchara; its use: recitation, for the pleasure of Sri Shanaishchara.
lines.6: On the head: salutation to the seer Sindhudvipa. On the mouth: salutation to the gayatri meter.
lines.7: On the heart: salutation to the deity Sri Shanaishchara.
lines.8: On the whole body: salutation to its use, for the pleasure of Sri Shanaishchara.
lines.9: May the son of the Sun protect my head; may Chhaya's son guard my forehead;
lines.10: may the hollow-eyed one protect my eyes; he who is dark as a peacock's neck, my ears;
lines.11: may the terrible one protect my nose; may Balimukha guard my mouth;
lines.12: may Samvartaka, the dissolver of worlds, protect my shoulders; may the giver of fear guard my arms;
lines.13: may Sauri protect my heart; may Shanaishchara guard my navel;
lines.14: may the king of planets protect my hips; the Sun's son, on every side;
lines.15: may the slow-going one protect my feet; may the dark one protect my whole body.
lines.16: Whoever recites daily this shield, armed with the strong names of Sauri,
lines.17: will be happy, blessed with children, and long-lived; there is no doubt of this.
